title: Outlet covers should block shocks without becoming a small choking piece
summary: CPSC says outlet covers and tamper-resistant receptacles help prevent electrical shock, and that a cover must not be easy for a child to pull off and choke on.
body: CPSC says outlet covers and outlet plates help protect children from electrical shock and possible electrocution. The cover should not be easy for a child to remove, and it should be large enough that a child cannot choke on it. If receptacles are being replaced, the page says to use a tamper-resistant type. That is a prevention device, not a rescue method. What to do after an electric shock is on the electrocution first-aid card. The advice is from a US product-safety page.
